overall: Violation found: the Board held eight executive sessions on disciplining Mr. Condez without the Purpose 1 notice and rights, mis-noticed the sessions, and could not withhold their minutes; the Board's July 31, 2014 cure was credited.

allegations.summary: Board met in eight executive sessions to discuss disciplining a police sergeant without notifying him or letting him attend, speak, or record the sessions.
allegations.key_passage: The Board failed to afford Mr. Condez any of the rights guaranteed to him by Purpose 1, including providing 48 hours written notice of the eight executive sessions during which it discussed disciplining him.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: meeting notices listed only 'Police Investigation' for executive sessions without citing the specific statutory purpose invoked.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the meeting notices identified the section of the Open Meeting Law dealing with executive sessions, G.L. c. 30A, § 21, but failed to identify which of the ten enumerated purposes the Board intended to invoke.

allegations.summary: Board withheld minutes of the eight executive sessions discussing the complainant, which the complainant sought.
allegations.key_passage: because the eight executive sessions were not held in compliance with G.L. c. 30A, § 21, the Board may not continue to withhold the minutes of these meetings under the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance by the Board with the Open Meeting Law; a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
Each Board member must review the Attorney General's executive session training video and certify compliance on the attached form within 30 days of receiving the determination.
Within 30 days, the Board must provide Mr. Condez the unredacted minutes portions discussing him from the eight executive sessions (Oct 7 2013 through Apr 7 2014).
remedy_passage: Immediate and future compliance by the Board with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
